note: Raw record of the engram-relaunch design workflow (2026-11-09): judge scores, the five concepts' red-team verdicts (3 lenses each), the critic report and the applied fixes. Supports docs/research/engram-relaunch-proposal.md.

rankings.name: Delta-Engram (training-free per-fact delta* rows, exact verified hash, presence gate; = assessment E0/E1)
rankings.time_to_decisive_signal: About 1-2 weeks. The concept estimates 5-10 GPU-h at 1-3 s per solve. The feasibility red-team estimates 2-15 s per solve on RDNA4 with CAM_NATIVE_GDN (unverified); at that rate, cut the plan down to 137 facts x 3 sites x 3 reps.
rankings.rationale: It is the only concept whose decisive experiment can actually falsify the Engram-site-on-a-frozen-base thesis, and it costs roughly nothing. Its premise is correct: every ~0.7 number in the repo was measured on a trained shared GatedMemoryTap (key-encoding §3.7-3.9), and no per-fact optimised delta* has ever been run here (engram-graft-assessment.md §3: E0 unrun). Three things count against it. (1) It is not novel. NeuralDB (2507.18028) already shows a flat-in-N gated per-fact residual on the CounterFact triad, and SWEA (2401.17809) already shows token-id-keyed subject embeddings at the input on a frozen base. Neither is cited anywhere in the repo's docs; I checked by grep. (2) Its RELAUNCH BAR is set against the wrong incumbent. It uses A1 logit-inject (0.876 solo, 0.565 at N=441, key-encoding §3.14/§6g), but the deployed system is the arm-B pointer, which is lossless by construction (RESULTS §7). (3) Its LOCALITY and FALSE-FIRE kills pass almost by construction, because CounterFact neighbours name different subjects (realedit.py:9). Its only real upside over the pointer is letting the model phrase the edit itself (format transfer and inflection). Every continuous carrier has walled at t>=1 (CAM_100_DISJOINT_RESULT), and the repo-evidence red-team argues the prior-confidence and object-vocabulary factors (r=-0.60, r=-0.89; §3.10-3.12) describe the downstream circuit and so should also hit delta*; the red-team itself marks this unverified for delta*. Literature (Mirage 2502.11177: ROME QAEdit 0.69 in the wild) suggests real-world reliability will not clearly beat exact forcing. The 35B write path needs a differentiable copy of about 70 GB, against 2x16 GB local, and HF-to-serve residual parity has never been measured (parity_spike.md status: plan only). Net: a high-value falsification arm and a weak core thesis.

rankings.name: Engram-Keyed Pointer (EKP): exact text-hash key + presence AND displacement trigger, pointer value at logits
rankings.time_to_decisive_signal: The proposed Stage 0/1 takes about 1 week and under 1 GPU-day, but as designed it is uninformative. A discriminating version, which moves alias, coreference, CounterFact+ and per-step serving cohorts into M0/M1, plus a 2-3 day minisgl TPOT spike, takes about 2-3 weeks.
rankings.rationale: It has the lowest risk and the highest continuity, and it keeps every measured escape: the lossless pointer (CAM_100 'THE UNLOCK'), output-site delivery (§3.14), and the presence gate (+0.464, RESULTS §8). It is not a relaunch. By its own admission and by kill 8 it is an evolution of arm B. Its Stage-1 test is tautological on this harness. probe_and_filter_counterfact keeps a record only when the base argmax equals true_ids[0] (recall_mag.py:739-770), so the displacement trigger always fires, and the different-subject neighbours never arm. The one discriminating axis, alias coverage, already has a published negative answer: subject-string gating on CounterFact gives 100% paraphrase activation but only 32% alias coverage, against 99.3% for a learned scope (2609.11063 SN13). The repo's one realistic routing measurement also found that key coverage on aliases is the bottleneck: retrieval 0.70, with the misses being same-structure aliases (scorecard finding 3). The displacement gate resembles ATBias (2406.12468), and the 'memory outside the circuit' thesis is SERAC's (2206.06520). On serving, per-decode-step triggering reverses the prefill-only store-read design that keeps decode graph-capturable (integration_design.md §5b/§5d). Its worth is as the key and front-end layer of the recommended hybrid, not as the core thesis.

rankings.name: Engram Cartridge: base-free normalized-text word-n-gram file, text-space ridge allocation, output delivery
rankings.time_to_decisive_signal: About 2 weeks of engineering plus 1-3 GPU-h, but C1 cannot discriminate as designed. It needs CounterFact+ prepended neighbours, same-subject other-relation, alias, and span-free serving cohorts to mean anything.
rankings.rationale: Its portability claim, one memory for any frozen model, is already a property of arm B, which is described as 'base-agnostic, training-free' with a string-edit source of truth (RESULTS §7; integration_design.md, rebuilding from the string list). The key design is already published in 2608.17050 (NFKC word-boundary n-gram hashing). With binary B, the 'text-space EngramEdit ridge' reduces to a bag-of-n-grams ridge classifier. Its relation AND-gate is a prompt-surface gate, which the repo measured as costly to generality: 0.611/0.667 against 0.907/0.926 for the store-confidence gate (RESULTS §7, 'Closing the gap'). A W=64 window scan would fire on every CounterFact+ prefixed neighbour (2305.17553) and would bring back the always-on hazard (key-encoding §3.20). Its kill criteria are near-tautological: pointer span_exact is true by construction (recall_mag.py:2419-2438), cross-base parity is guaranteed because the key never touches the base, and the token-id 2-gram strawman stands in for the bypass test. It does contribute three useful pieces: a (subject, relation) key that closes online_api.md §1.2, an auditable file format for the edit plane, and negative-row allocation as an offline false-fire calibrator.

rankings.name: CF-Engram: calibrated per-base Engram fusion reader (W_Q/W_K/W_V, alpha_t, conv) at L2 + per-fact row solves
rankings.time_to_decisive_signal: The plan says 3-4 weeks and 25-35 GPU-h. The feasibility red-team re-estimates a few hundred GPU-h, based on about 1 s per step measured with backward above L24 only (DIARY Phase 16), against full-depth backward from L2.
rankings.rationale: It reverses both escapes the repo measured: back from the lossless pointer to a continuous value, and back from logits to the earliest residual site, where L3 garbles (scorecard F2; RESULTS §10). Its key justification is that a calibrated reader generalises to held-out relations. The repo measured the opposite twice: trained readouts deliver 0.000 on novel relations against 0.77 in-distribution (key-encoding §3.23), and ripple drops from 0.85 to 0.31 on a held-out relation (scorecard F3). So the CALIBRATION/RELATION-SHORTCUT kill is the predicted outcome, and the concept itself says so. Its training-free A3 core is SWEA (2401.17809), and its calibrated-editor idea is close to REMEDI (2304.00740), whose essence score of 24.8 shows a trained early editor did not fix same-subject bleed. Its SITE KILL requires both metrics to fall below 0.70 while the concept expects per-fact solves to 'work trivially', so it is effectively unfireable. The 35B write and calibration path has no hardware home on 2x16 GB. The one idea worth keeping is the SSOR (same-subject other-relation) and SNG cohorts, with relation selectivity as the single science question.

rankings.name: Read-Port Retrofit (Mode B): world-swap co-train a 1.7-4B checkpoint to read a hashed table, then freeze
rankings.time_to_decisive_signal: About 2-4 weeks and $100-250 of cloud H100 (35-40 H100-h claimed). The feasibility red-team estimates 30-110 H100-h for evaluation alone without a batched delta* solver. A negative result at 200M tokens cannot be told apart from under-training, since STAPLE trains for about 200B tokens.
rankings.rationale: It is the only concept with a credible path to integration and ripple above injection, and its science question (is the wall frozen-ness or the site?) has not been tested with a trained backbone. Against it: it drops the project's defining invariants (frozen base, attach-anywhere, remove the organ, the deployed 35B). The repo already answers its premise the other way: on the same frozen base, the logit site moved solo from 0.65 to 0.876 (key-encoding §3.14, §0(C)), and ROME-style v* reaches about 99.9 on frozen GPT-J (as cited via Larimar 2403.11901, Table 2). That makes A0 likely to saturate and the A0-vs-A2 contrast uninformative. Prior art covers the thesis: Larimar (train once, closed-form writes, exact forget), KBLaM (2410.10450, synthetic-KB reader training), and LTE (2402.11905, its A3 control). The early L2 port is negative even in a native Engram model (2606.19172 §4.3, reported but unverified). Every threshold it uses was measured on Qwen3.5-4B with the pipeline it discards. The cheap E0/E1 ladder that would decide whether this is needed has not been run. It should be held as a conditional follow-up, not a relaunch.

judge.recommended_core:
I would not relaunch memory-organ around Engram. The core should stay the deployed arm-B pointer: an exact object-token-id value, delivered at the output with presence gating (RESULTS §7; CAM_100_DISJOINT 'THE UNLOCK'; RESULTS §8). Every one of the 15 red-team verdicts refuted its concept at major severity. The finding that recurs, backed by the repo's own measurements, is that each concept beats only A1, the trained out_proj logit-inject path (0.81 to 0.565, key-encoding §0(D)/§6g). None was compared with the deployed pointer, which has no shared readout and is exact by construction.

The recommended core is a two-track hybrid.

Track 1, evolution (taken from EKP and the Cartridge): put an Engram-style key front end on arm B.
- A salted, fingerprinted key over normalized text, keyed on (subject, relation). It runs hash-first and falls back to whitened GTE at the 0.90 gate.
- The hit bit becomes the provenance and presence signal.
- Per-position prefix keys over the emitted object replace the _gen_ptr cursor.
- Exact delete, plus an auditable cartridge file as the edit-plane export format.
- This keeps base-agnosticism, millisecond writes, KV-cache invariance and losslessness. It closes online_api.md §1.2 (one live value per subject) and integration_design.md §7 risk #1 (explicit subject span).

Track 2, falsification (taken from Delta-Engram, as arm E0/E1/E2 of engram-graft-assessment.md §3): one bounded, training-free experiment that settles whether a frozen circuit reads per-fact hashed residual rows.
- Rows are raw d_model delta*, stored under an exact verified hash, at l in {embed, 2, 8, 16, 24}.
- E1 compares raw-d rows against a fixed r=512 projection and against the trained out_proj, to test the shared-readout diagnosis.
- A NeuralDB-style activation-cosine gate (gamma=0.65, 2507.18028) is the in-run control, so the key type is the only variable.
- The deployed pointer runs in the same session on the same cohorts.
- Present it as 'NeuralDB/SWEA with an exact verified token-span key', not as Engram.

The Engram brand, early-site fusion, the trained context gate and co-training (CF-Engram, Mode B) all stay parked until Track 2 produces a specific outcome; the conditions are in go_no_go. The repo's own record argues against them: a ~0.7 residual wall (§3.7-3.11), early L3 garbling (scorecard F2), relation-specific trained readouts (§3.23, F3), and no frozen-backbone Engram graft anywhere in the literature (assessment §1).
ideas_to_graft_from_others: PRECONDITION FOR ALL ARMS (raised by every red-team): measure the deployed arm-B pointer on the CounterFact triad at N=441 and N=1105 with 3 reps, inside the harness. tools/bakeoff_abc.py and cam/export_serving.py, both cited by RESULTS §7 and §8, are absent from this checkout (verified with ls), so no comparator for the incumbent currently exists. Every relaunch bar must be stated against arm B, not against A1's 0.565.

From CF-Engram: the SSOR cohort (same subject, other relation; templates disjoint between solve and eval) and the SNG cohort (next-token KL after incidental n-gram hits in generic text). Make SSOR the primary locality metric for any subject-keyed write, because DEP neighbours name other subjects and are near-vacuous for exact keys (realedit.py:9).
From CF-Engram: the Phase-0 CPU writability and frequency screen (fraction of subjects with a writable 2/3-gram after the frequency cut; out-of-store hit rate against the pointer's 0.05).

From Delta-Engram: the E1 shared-readout test (raw-d rows vs a fixed random r=512 projection vs the trained out_proj, N=137 to 441). It directly confirms or refutes key-encoding §0(D), which is an inference and not a measurement.
From Delta-Engram: an 'exact no-op on miss' logit byte-identity test and a CPU/GPU hasher-parity test in tests/test_smoke.py.

From Delta-Engram feasibility salvage: measure delta*-solve wall-clock on 20 records on RDNA4, and spot-check on cloud whether deltas solved in HF bf16 survive the served 35B numerics, by adapting the parity_spike.md probe, which has never been run. Do both before any scale run.

From EKP: stateless per-position prefix keys over the emitted object ids as a replacement for the _gen_ptr cursor. Also from EKP: normalized-text keys, which close the alternate-tokenization bypass (2609.29045; the 38.6% figure is from a secondary summary and unverified). Use NFD with mark stripping, because NFKC+casefold does not strip diacritics.

From EKP: the o_old-rank displacement gate, but only as an ablation measured per position in free generation and multi-turn contexts, and against an ATBias-style rank-constrained bias (2406.12468). On the validity-gated harness o_old is rank 0 by construction (recall_mag.py:739-770).

From the Cartridge: a (subject, relation) key used as a disambiguator only when one subject has more than one live relation, never as an AND gate on every fire. The repo measured a 0.611 vs 0.907 generality cost for prompt-surface gates (RESULTS §7).

From the Cartridge: negative-row text-space ridge allocation as an offline false-fire calibrator for shared n-grams, and the .mocart-style auditable, provenance-carrying file as the snapshot/export format (online_api.md §1-§4). Auditability is relevant to BadEngram (2609.13478).

From Mode B: the A3 'LoRA-only / pliable residual' control logic (it separates 'the table is read' from 'the residual became editable'), an empty-table capability check, and held-out-relation efficacy as the primary metric. Use these only if Track 2 stalls.

From all literature red-teams: add CounterFact+ prefixed-neighbour prompts (2305.17553), RippleEdits/UniEdit subject-alias cohorts (2307.12976, 2505.12345), coreference/multi-turn prompts, and a powered (at least 150 prompts) format-transfer/free-generation cohort. The 12-prompt gen-coherence set (9/12 baseline) has a standard error of about 0.13.

From the EKP/Cartridge feasibility salvage: a 2-3 day minisgl serving spike that puts any per-decode-step trigger in the graph-captured sampler as static buffers under TP=2, with kill if TPOT overhead exceeds a few percent or a per-step host sync is needed. The prefill-only store read exists for capture safety (integration_design.md §5b/§5d).

Dossier hygiene. The 'systems inventory' and 'literature inventory' cited throughout the dossier do not exist in the repo (grep finds no *.md matches), so the claims resting on them (zero extra collectives, 1-5 s/edit sidecar, 3-14 h bulk import, the 'empty cell' gap verdict) are unverified. The '~46% multi-token' figure is from the non-validity-gated bake-off set (RESULTS.md:538). Full-CounterFact multi-token supply is 2.7% (key-encoding:799), and the base-known filter yields about 1 per 137 (§3.28). Multi-token cohorts must therefore be built outside the base-known filter or they are underpowered.

redteam.name: Delta-Engram: a training-free hashed residual-patch memory (frozen everything; zero shared trained parameters)
redteam.thesis: Each fact is one isolated row: a per-edit delta* (d_model) solved with the base frozen, stored under an exact verified hash of the subject's token n-gram, added at the subject's last token at one mid-early residual layer only on a hit. No bind, tap, fusion or shared readout exists, so (a) efficacy should be flat in N, because the shared-readout bottleneck blamed for 0.81 -> 0.565 at N=441 (key-encoding §0(D), §6g) is gone, and (b) the frozen circuit produces the object itself, multi-token included, with no answer-span scoping. The repo's ~0.7 residual wall was measured on a TRAINED SHARED tap (key-encoding §3.7-3.9), never on a per-fact optimized delta.

verdicts.salvage:
Run it as arm E0, not as a relaunch, and change the comparison to the incumbent that is actually deployed:
(1) Add the deployed whitened-GTE pointer (with seed-once/answer-span delivery) to the in-run baselines for efficacy, generality and span-exact. Drop the trained-tap 0.565 as the reference for the 'flat in N' claim, because the pointer is already flat in N by construction.
(2) Pre-register the claim only where the pointer is structurally weak:
- a format-transfer cohort (QA phrasing, object-not-next-token, inflection), scored by a judge on free generation;
- a powered multi-token cohort, built from facts outside the base-known filter (private-demo invented objects plus CounterFact objects at CAM_MAX_OBJ_TOK up to 4), because §3.19 gives only ~2.7% supply.
(3) Run the prior-strength test early: per-fact delta* at the best layer on the always-FAIL / high-P(orig) / large-vocab (P159) subset, plus one larger or more knowledgeable base. §3.11 predicts this is where residual values die and the pointer does not.
(4) Add a same-subject essence cohort as the primary locality metric.
If delta* only wins on format transfer, keep the exact verified hash and its presence bit (the genuinely new key-side asset) bolted onto the pointer/logit value path. Use delta* rows as an optional 'phrase-it-yourself' value type for single-hop facts, rather than relaunching the concept around them.

verdicts.objection:
Read through the literature, this concept is not new, and it is not Engram. Once the Engram parts are stripped out, the core thesis has already been published as NeuralDB (arXiv 2507.18028, ICLR 2026). The concept strips out all of the following:
- multi-head hashing;
- the context gate alpha_t;
- the short conv;
- CPU offload;
- the fixed early site;
- n-gram allocation, which survives only in side arm E2.

What remains is a per-fact residual delta on a frozen base, stored in a gated table and added at one FFN or residual layer. NeuralDB already does this:
- The delta is solved with the ROME-style NLL over random prefixes plus a "{subject} is a" KL term, which is the same as the concept's WRITE step.
- It is stored as one isolated row per fact in a gated KV table, with no shared trained readout.
- It is added at one mid-early layer (l = 7 or 8), and only when a gate fires.
- It is evaluated on the CounterFact triad.
- Results:
  - Efficacy is flat in N: 99.9 to 99.2 going from 2k to 10k edits on Llama-3-8B. Generalization is 86.6 to 85.9 and specificity 88.2 to 85.6.
  - On ZsRE it reaches 95.5 efficacy at 100k edits.

So both headline claims are pre-empted:
- (a) "Isolated rows make efficacy flat in N."
- (b) "A per-fact optimized delta escapes the ~0.7 wall." ROME single-edit reliability is 98.7 synthetic on Llama-3-8B (2502.11177, Table 3).

GRACE (2211.11031) already offers a discrete per-edit codebook on a frozen model. SUIT (2509.24502) adds a gradient-optimized residual at the subject's last token. The only real difference left is the gate: an exact hash of the subject's token span instead of NeuralDB's activation cosine above gamma = 0.65. That is a key-type swap, and it is not new either:
- Memory Grafting (2605.20948) already uses an exact integer n-gram map.
- The repo already uses md5 subject banks (key-encoding §0(A)).

The concept says the cell "frozen backbone + grafted table + fact writes on the CounterFact triad" is empty, citing a "literature inventory §(b)". No such file exists in the repo, and the claim is false once "Engram" is dropped from the description. Nor does the Engram literature support the mechanism on a frozen backbone:
- EngramEdit (2610.10533) relies on LongCat's 31.4B natively pretrained n-gram table.
- STAPLE (2610.12599) trains the backbone on about 200B tokens.
- Memory Grafting pretrains its recipient from scratch on 50-100B tokens.
- An independent frozen-base Engram replication (github.com/t-hertel/Engram, unverified) reports zero downstream gain.

So "relaunch around Engram" is branding over ROME/NeuralDB.

On whether it beats keeping the current system, the evidence does not clearly favour it:
- Under realistic evaluation, ROME-class per-fact deltas fall to 69.1 reliability and 57.0 generalization on QAEdit with Llama-3-8B (2502.11177, Table 3). Even the best case stays below the pointer's lossless 1.00 isolated exact delivery (CAM_100_DISJOINT).
- ROME and MEMIT show large specificity failures when the edited subject appears in context (CounterFact+, 2305.17553), and factual drift in long-form text (2402.09394). This design maximises exactly that exposure: it fires on every mention of the subject, for every relation.
- Exact token keys are bypassed by non-canonical tokenizations about 38.6% of the time (2609.29045; figure from a secondary summary, unverified).
- In exchange it gives up base portability, which is the project's north star, plus lossless values and millisecond writes.
verdicts.salvage:
Do not relaunch the project around this. Position it honestly as "NeuralDB/GRACE with an exact verified token-span key", and run it as arm D inside the existing presence-gated system, as engram-graft-assessment.md §3 already recommends. Six changes would make the experiment publishable rather than a replication:

1. Run NeuralDB itself (activation-cosine gate at gamma = 0.65, same delta solve) as the in-run baseline, so the only variable is the key type: exact hash versus activation cosine.
2. Score with the harness's argmax metric plus Mirage-style wild, autoregressive evaluation (2502.11177), not P(new) > P(old).
3. Add the CounterFact+ prepended-subject specificity cohort (2305.17553) and a non-canonical-tokenization bypass cohort (2609.29045). These are the failure modes an always-on-subject trigger is most exposed to.
4. Keep the pointer as the delivery path. Promote the delta only as the "model-phrased, format-transfer" path, and only if it beats the pointer on format-transfer and multi-token tasks.
5. Drop the "Engram" name, because none of Engram's components survive.
6. Restore the north-star invariant by keying on normalised text strings, and treat delta rows as a cache that is re-solved per base.

The one genuinely untested question that is worth the GPU hours is whether an exact presence bit can replace NeuralDB's cosine threshold and remove its fluency/specificity trade-off at 10^4 edits on a GDN/MoE base.

verdicts.objection: On feasibility the concept splits into two parts. Only the cheap part can actually be built, and passing it would not decide the relaunch. (1) The offline E0-TF on Qwen3.5-4B can be built on one 16 GB RDNA4 card from the existing harness. Every cited code anchor checks out. But the concept wants to be the new core thesis, and the deployed product is a frozen Qwen3.6-35B-A3B under TP=2 on the same two 16 GB gfx1201 cards. Those cards are leased in turn between serving and research. A per-edit delta* needs autograd through the deployed base. A bf16 35B (about 70 GB) cannot be held differentiably on 2x16 GB: the 9B (about 18 GB) already needed both cards. The serve stack runs inference only, and is most likely quantized (inferred, unverified). Deltas would also have to be solved on a different numeric path (HF bf16, or cloud CUDA/fla) than the one that consumes them (minisgl HIP). That HF-vs-serve residual parity has never been measured; the parity spike is a plan only. The deployed pointer forces tokens and does not depend on residual parity at all. M8 and M9, the parts that make this a relaunch, therefore cannot run on project hardware. Online writes would also need a third GPU or a pause in serving. (2) The decisive experiment's bars are set against the wrong incumbent. RELAUNCH BAR compares to the trained logit-inject arm (0.876 solo / 0.565 at N=441), not to the deployed pointer (exact-id delivery, 1.00 isolated, false-fire 0.05). LOCALITY and verified-key FALSE-FIRE are close to passing by construction, because a miss is a byte-exact no-op and CounterFact neighbours name other subjects; the concept admits this. Efficacy on the rewrite prompt is mostly a re-run of ROME's optimized v*. So a 'pass' mainly shows that ROME-in-a-dict works on a 4B. It does not show the concept beats keeping the pointer. The one comparison that could favour Delta-Engram over the pointer (phrasing / format transfer / multi-token in free generation) is pushed to M4 and judged on the 12-prompt gen-coherence set against 9/12 (n=12, SE about 0.13). (3) Several cost and serving claims cite a 'systems inventory §3-§10' and a 'literature inventory §(b)' that do not exist in the repo: the bulk-import 3-14 h figure, the 2-4 week integration estimate, and 'zero extra collectives'. The compute estimate also leaves out the in-run trained baselines at N=1105, which have never been run (only N=441, n=1, exists).
verdicts.salvage: Do not relaunch. Run E0-TF as a cheap, training-free arm (assessment arm D) that tests key-encoding §0(D), and change three things. (a) Re-anchor the bar on the deployed pointer, not the trained logit-inject. The only claim worth a relaunch is 'the frozen circuit phrases or inflects or embeds the edit where pointer forcing fails'. Make that the primary pre-registered metric: a format-transfer and free-generation cohort of at least 100-200 prompts, judged span-exact against _gen_ptr, not the 12-prompt set. (b) Move a deployment-feasibility gate ahead of M2. Measure delta-solve wall-clock on 20 records on the RDNA4 card. Then run one cloud spot check (a single 80 GB+ GPU for under an hour) that solves deltas on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and replays them through the actual quantized minisgl TP=2 serve model, by adapting the never-run parity_spike probe to the chosen layer. If deltas solved in HF bf16 do not survive the serve numerics, the 35B relaunch is dead whatever the 4B result. (c) If the science passes but (b) fails, keep the hashed verified key as a prefetch / presence-bit front end for the existing pointer and logit-inject value path, and offer Delta-Engram rows only as a batch-solved, 4B-served (integration_design MVP base) option for edits the pointer cannot phrase.

redteam.name: CF-Engram: calibrated-fusion hashed-row memory for frozen LLMs ("Mode A proper")
redteam.thesis: Fit one small Engram-style fusion reader per frozen base, once, on a few hundred MB of synthetic-entity and generic text, then freeze it. Every fact write after that is a per-row solve through the frozen base plus the frozen reader into an exact-key, CPU-offloadable 2/3-gram table. The bet is that a calibrated reader makes an early additive token-keyed channel readable and relation-selective where a raw residual write is not, and that isolated per-fact rows remove the shared-readout loss that takes efficacy from 0.81 to 0.55 between N=137 and N=441 (key-encoding §0(D)).

verdicts.objection:
CF-Engram reverses both escapes that the repo has measured as working, and it is aimed at a scale problem the deployed system does not have.

(1) Value. The repo already went from lossy continuous values to an exact token-id pointer, and the pointer was the fix. Four readout levers were falsified at a per-token floor of about 0.50 for t≥1, even with one value in a fresh store. The pointer then hit 1.00 per-token and 4/4 span-exact standing (CAM_100_DISJOINT_RESULT.md, "Lever 1/3/4" and "THE UNLOCK"). CF-Engram replaces that lossless value with a solved continuous row read through the frozen circuit.

(2) Site. CF-Engram moves delivery back from logits to the earliest residual site. The residual ceiling of about 0.7 survived seven levers, and fidelity rises with depth (L18 0.565 < L24 0.69 ≈ L28 0.70). Early L3 garbles (key-encoding §3.7–3.10; scorecard). Leaving the residual site is what broke the ceiling (0.65 → 0.876, §3.14).

(3) Motivation. The relaunch's stated reason is that private rows remove the shared-readout loss (0.81 → 0.55 from N=137 to 441, key-encoding §0(D), §6g). That loss belongs to the tap/out_proj logit-inject path. The deployed arm B pointer already stores per-fact, isolated, exact object ids with no shared readout (RESULTS §7). So isolation is already in production, with no loss at all.

As a result, the concept's own GO bars (efficacy ≥0.81 at N=441, span-exact ≥0.75) sit below what the deployed pointer already measures (span-exact 1.00 on #100, and counterfactual delivery 0.92 with 48 multi-token objects coexisting). Its INCUMBENT KILL is benchmarked against A1 logit-inject, not against the deployed pointer. Even a full GO would therefore not show that it beats keeping the current system, and it would give up base-agnosticism, training-free writes and millisecond writes along the way.

The representational advantages it claims are also predicted to fail by repo data:
- Earliest-site rows let every later layer consume the edit: injection does not integrate (KV-append 0.000; every write op at every depth is below RAG; early L3 garbles).
- A calibrated reader generalises to held-out relations: trained readouts are relation-specific shortcuts (0.000 on novel relations, §3.23; 0.85 → 0.31 ripple on a held-out relation, scorecard F3).

The one gap in this refutation: the repo has never measured per-fact optimised residual rows. Every residual-wall number comes from a trained, shared tap.

The literature already fills the "empty cell" this relaunch claims, and it also undercuts the premise that justifies the calibrated reader.

1. **The training-free core is SWEA.** SWEA (arXiv 2401.17809, AAAI 2025) runs on a frozen base. It caches a per-subject private embedding under a key made of the subject's exact token ids, finds the longest matching id run, and adds the embedding to the subject positions at the input (ℓ=0). That embedding is solved per edit with KL plus NLL of the new target over P model-generated prefixes. This is CF-Engram's A3 arm and its write rule, minus the 2/3-gram hashing and the ridge penalty. SWEA reports CounterFact efficacy/generalization/specificity at 10,000 edits of 99.6/98.3/79.0 on GPT-J and 98.4/93.5/79.3 on Llama-2.
2. **The calibrated-reader idea has a precedent in REMEDI.** REMEDI (arXiv 2304.00740, COLM 2024) trains a small editor once, with only the editor's W and b updated. It adds the result at layer 1 at the last entity token on GPT-J and gets CounterFact efficacy 98.2 and neighborhood 100. The authors report that early layers worked best.
3. **So frozen circuits demonstrably read early additive subject-position channels.** That holds both per-fact (SWEA) and amortized (REMEDI). The repo's ~0.7 wall was measured on a trained, shared residual tap (key-encoding §0(C), §3.7–3.11), not on per-fact solves. The concept's own expected_failure_mode (1) already concedes this.
4. **EngramEdit is mechanically the same input-level operation.** It averages n-gram vectors with the token embedding and adds updates to the embedding output (2610.10533 App. B.4.1/B.4.3, sum fusion). It never compares against SWEA, GRACE, WISE, MEMOIR or MEMIT; its baselines are FT, FT-L, AdaLoRA, UnKE, MoEEdit and Memory-FT.
5. **What is left as new is narrow.** It is a calibrated, relation-selective gate (the W_Q path) aimed at same-subject-other-relation bleed. That bleed is SWEA's own documented weak axis: RippleEdits relation specificity 0.41 vs MEMIT 0.48 on GPT-J (2401.17809). It is also REMEDI's: essence 24.8 vs prefix 40.5 (2304.00740 Table 3). No paper shows that layer-2 query states encode the relation (unverified), and REMEDI's trained editor did not fix essence. That is one incremental ablation, not a new core thesis.
6. **The motivating gap belongs to the wrong system.** The 0.81→0.55 shared-readout loss (key-encoding §0(D)) comes from the trained product-key/out_proj logit-inject path (A1). The DEPLOYED incumbent is the arm-B GTE pointer. Its delivery is exact by construction, equal to addressing, and multi-token by nature, with false-fire 0.05 (RESULTS §7 bake-off).
7. **The relaunch would trade those properties away.** It gives up losslessness, millisecond writes, base-agnosticism and KV-cache independence. In return it targets a capacity loss the deployed system does not have, and its INCUMBENT KILL is measured against A1 rather than against the pointer.

Net: this is not clearly better than keeping the current system, and its novelty claim as written is false.
verdicts.salvage:
Do not relaunch. Run the idea as a bounded arm D inside the existing harness, with the deployed pointer (arm B) as the incumbent to beat, not A1.

1. **Rename Phase 1 honestly.** Call it "SWEA/EngramEdit-style token-keyed input rows on Qwen3.5-4B". Add SWEA (and, where feasible, REMEDI and GRACE) as literature baselines. Expect high efficacy and generality on subject-preserving CounterFact paraphrases; the published numbers predict this already.
2. **Make relation selectivity the single scientific question.** The SSOR cohort, same subject with another relation, is where SWEA (RippleEdits relation specificity 0.41) and REMEDI (essence 24.8) both fail. The question is whether a once-calibrated relation-selective gate (the W_Q windowed path) fixes SSOR bleed without losing efficacy. Pre-register CALIBRATION KILL against a SWEA-objective A3 at the same site. If it passes, that is a publishable incremental result.
3. **Keep what the repo uniquely has, as components.**
   - The exact-hash presence/provenance bit (RESULTS §8, +0.464), bolted onto the pointer.
   - Per-position object n-gram keys for the multi-token wall (#100).
4. **Add the tokenization-robustness cohort.** Include the alternative-tokenization bypass check from 2609.29045 as an explicit kill, because exact-id keys inherit it.

verdicts.objection:
On the feasibility lens, CF-Engram cannot write facts on the hardware it is supposed to deploy to. Separately, its decisive experiment would not show that it beats the system already deployed.

(1) The write path does not fit the serving box. Every write is an autograd solve through the frozen base from layer ℓ≈2 to the output. Rows are base-specific, so the solve must run through the exact base being served: the 35B MoE under TP=2. The serving box has 2×16 GB = 32 GB.
- A 35B model in bf16 is about 70 GB (arithmetic). Serving it in 32 GB therefore implies a quantized serve checkpoint. The repo never records the serving precision (unverified).
- minisgl's forward is inference-only. Making it differentiable is the parity spike's "last resort" option (parity_spike.md §4(d)).
- A backward pass through a quantized MoE in HF on ROCm is unverified. It would also have to share 32 GB with the running engine.
- Reader calibration on the 35B ("1–2 days on the TP=2 box") hits the same memory wall.
- The "1–5 s/edit sidecar" and "systems inventory §5" sources the concept cites do not exist in the repo (grep finds no systems, literature or evidence inventory).
- Compare the incumbent: a pointer write is a GTE encode plus an id insert, and it is base-agnostic (RESULTS §7). The relaunch swaps that millisecond, portable write for a write with no hardware home. Every base upgrade would also force a reader recalibration plus re-solving every stored edit.

(2) The cost estimate is off by roughly an order of magnitude. The plan assumes about 3 s per 25–50-step solve, which needs about 67 TFLOP/s sustained at about 300 tokens on RDNA4.
- The repo's own measurement is stage-2 = 147 s for 150 steps, about 1 s per step (DIARY "hardware detour"). That run backpropagated only through the layers above L24. An ℓ=2 solve backpropagates through nearly the whole stack.
- At that measured rate a solve is about 25–90 s, not 3 s.
- Phase 1 alone is 441–1105 facts × 5 sites × 3 reps. Phase 2 needs fresh solves for A4, A4-local and A4-rawd, because each changes the optimum. Then the Qwen3-4B-Base replication doubles everything.
- My estimate is therefore a few hundred GPU-h on 2 shared, flake-prone cards, against the plan's 25–35 GPU-h. The project's prior full investigation cost about $2 (RESULTS §10), and a "~3 min" run was already called unaffordable at factorial scale (key-encoding §6b).

(3) The decisive experiment is not decisive against the current system.
- INCUMBENT KILL and the GO bars are set against A1 (hard-gated logit inject). The deployed system is arm B, the pointer (RESULTS §7). The pointer delivers exactly whenever it is addressed, and it is multi-token by nature. The concept itself credits the pointer with span-exact 1.00.
- GO only requires efficacy ≥0.81 and span-exact ≥0.75. A design can pass GO while being worse than what already ships.
- A2 is only "reference numbers": it is never run in the harness on the SSOR, SNG or generality cohorts. Those are the only axes where CF-Engram claims an edge (relation selectivity; online_api §1.2 keys the deployed design on subject alone).
- The DEP-keep cohort contains different subjects, which an exact-hash key misses trivially, so that cohort cannot discriminate.
- The SITE KILL needs efficacy <0.70 AND generality <0.70. The concept's own expected_failure_mode (1) says per-fact free solves will "probably work trivially", so this kill is effectively unfireable.
- The result is that most of the spend reaches Phase 2 without ever testing the question that matters: is this better than keeping the pointer?
verdicts.salvage:
Do not relaunch. Run the assessment's own ladder as arm D, with the deployed pointer measured inside the harness.
1. Keep the pointer as the core.
2. Run Phase 0 (the CPU n-gram writability and false-fire screen) and the training-free A3 site sweep on Qwen3.5-4B only. Budget it from the measured ~1 s/step, not 3 s per solve: subsample to about 137 facts × {0, 2, 16} sites × 3 reps.
3. Add the pointer (A2), plus a relation-tagged pointer variant (online_api §1.2 'Full'), to the SSOR, SNG and generality cohorts.
4. Make GO require beating A2 on SSOR-keep and on generality at non-inferior efficacy and span-exact.
5. Do per-base reader calibration and any 35B write path only if A3 already beats the pointer on SSOR at 4B. Before that, cost a write box that can hold the served 35B with gradients; the current 2×16 GB box cannot.

If A3 fails, keep only the key-side wins inside the existing pointer/logit path: exact hashed keys for prefetch, the presence bit, and the provenance bit.

redteam.name: Engram-Keyed Pointer (EKP): memory addressed by the token stream and delivered at the output
redteam.thesis: Keep the part of Engram the repo's evidence supports, the deterministic O(1) key read off the token stream (a presence bit, CPU-side, per-position). Drop the part the evidence predicts will fail: an early additive residual site read by a frozen circuit. The key drives the already-proven lossless pointer value at the output logits, gated by key presence AND by the base's own 'the old object belongs here' signal. Honest verdict: this is an evolution of the mechanism (a key swap plus a new trigger on deployed arm B). It counts as a relaunch only of the thesis: memory-organ stops claiming 'the frozen circuit reads a memory channel' and claims instead 'a frozen LLM's editable memory is a token-addressed exact table outside the circuit, with the circuit used as the gate rather than the reader'.

verdicts.objection:
The repo's own results predict EKP will not be clearly better than the deployed arm B. What EKP would actually change is untested, and the one realistic routing measurement the repo has points the wrong way.

(1) The value, the site and the delivery are already deployed. Arm B is the GTE pointer: exact object ids, forced at the output, rank-authoritative (RESULTS §7 bake-off; ROADMAP.md:72-77). The pointer already solved the multi-token t≥1 wall: isolated 1.00, standing 4/4 span-exact (CAM_100_DISJOINT_RESULT 'THE UNLOCK').

(2) EKP's headline efficacy claim, "removes the shared out_proj blamed for the N=441 drop", is made against the wrong opponent. The 0.81→0.55 drop (key-encoding §0(D)) belongs to the out_proj path, which here is the A1 conf-gated logit inject. The deployed pointer never had an out_proj; its "delivery-exact = addressing by construction" (RESULTS §7). Kill criterion 3 is therefore benchmarked against a strawman (A1 at 0.565). The real comparator, A2, should already sit near ceiling.

(3) Addressing is already solved: below-gate 0/441 with K1 (key-encoding §0(D), §3.16). Generality on CounterFact is "free by design because retrieval is subject-keyed" (§3.17), and paraphrases keep the subject string. So on the triad, A3 ≈ A2 is predicted by the repo's own logic. The concept's kill criterion 8 is very likely to fire, and the concept's own expected_failure_mode says so.

(4) Where the two keys do differ, the evidence goes against EKP. The only measured routed bank under realistic keys topped out at router retrieval 0.70 with "honest subject-keys; misses are same-structure aliases" (frozen-base-titans-scorecard.md finding 3; RESULTS §10). So key coverage is the binding limit in practice, and an exact canonical-text hash covers strictly fewer aliases than whitened GTE.

(5) The new trigger, "the base's o_old in top-5", rests on a premise the repo undercuts for its own stated use case:
- That use case is facts the base cannot know (key-encoding §3.22, §3.23).
- The write gate stores only when the object is not the base's top-1 (RESULTS §8 rank gate).
- For novel subjects the base's "old object" is a generic default. The repo's examples show 'English' for Oleg Kotov, Zephyrina Quillsworth and Bartholomew Fizzwick (§3.29; CAM_100_DISJOINT_RESULT table).
- For base-known edits, the priors are weak (P 0.17–0.48, RESULTS §8).

So displacement collapses to "a common token is in top-5", or falls back to brittle relation-template matching. Neither has been measured.

(6) The renamed thesis, "the circuit is the gate, not the reader", is not new. The repo already concluded that injection cannot integrate (scorecard F2; RESULTS §10), and it already ships an out-of-circuit exact table. Retiring the founding claim is a documentation change, not a new core thesis.

Net: on the repo's evidence this is at best a systems evolution of arm B, a cheaper encoder-free key that needs no subject span. It is not a relaunch that beats the current system.
verdicts.salvage:
Recast EKP as an evolution of deployed arm B, not a relaunch: a hash-first, whitened-GTE-fallback key on the existing pointer, keeping GTE as the alias safety net.

Make the go/no-go hinge on the axes the triad cannot see:
- Run Stage 0 with A2 (arm B) as the only comparator, not A1. Drop the 0.565 incumbent baseline.
- Score on the stress cohorts the repo's realistic routing measurement implicates: aliases and same-structure aliases (scorecard finding 3), coreference and multi-turn prompts, and same-subject other-relation prompts.
- Report false-fire on general text for the displacement gate, with o_old drawn from the base's actual default for novel subjects (e.g. 'English').
- Upgrade the key to (subject, relation) rows to close the one-value-per-subject limit (online_api.md §1.2).

Ship it only if it removes the explicit-subject requirement on the 35B deployment at a false-fire rate no worse than arm B's 0.05 without losing alias recall. Otherwise keep the current system unchanged.

verdicts.objection:
EKP's proposed new core has already been published and measured: an exact, normalised subject-string gate that releases a stored edit at query time, with the base unchanged otherwise. The published numbers show the same failure EKP lists as its own risk. Picozzi (arXiv 2609.11063, Supplementary Note 13) gates CounterFact edits with "the rule activates when a prompt contains the edit subject after light text normalisation". Results:
- 100% paraphrase activation and 0.2% neighbourhood activation, with S=100 (ES/PS/NS 100/100/100) on 100 edits.
- Only 32% subject-alias coverage, against 99.3% for a learned scope classifier.

So EKP's Stage 1 CounterFact triad is uninformative by construction. EKP's own "expected failure mode" concedes this, and the literature has already run it. The only discriminating axis, alias and surface coverage, has a published answer that predicts EKP trips its own KEY-COVERAGE kill against the GTE key.

The rest of the stack also has priority:
- **Memory plus scope gate, override at output, base untouched, reusable across bases:** SERAC (2206.06520, sections 3.1 and 5.2), including its training-free hidden-state lookup-cache baseline (LU, Appendix B).
- **"Displacement trigger" and o_old damping:** ATBias (2406.12468, sections 3.1-3.4). It gets the parametric answer by an offline cloze probe, restricts biasing to tokens in the base's top-k (k=10) that match an entity, then boosts new-knowledge tokens (λ_n=25) and suppresses parametric ones.
- **Per-position prefix-key continuation:** CPU suffix-match drafting (REST 2311.08252) and source-match-then-force-target terminology decoding (1704.07138; Dinu et al. 1906.01105).

Engram supplies nothing load-bearing:
- EKP drops Engram's actual mechanism, a conditional memory the circuit learns to read (2601.07372 §2.3).
- What remains is a hashed suffix dictionary lookup.
- The EngramEdit statistic EKP borrows describes a different failure. The 48 of 49 efficacy failures (97.96%) in shared rows come from "different targets may require conflicting changes to the same parameters" (2610.10533 App. C.3.3). That is value conflict in continuous shared rows, which EKP's private, ref-counted rows cannot have. It is not evidence about false-fires.

Calling this an "Engram relaunch" is therefore not supported by the Engram literature. The thesis that remains, "an editable exact table outside the circuit, with the circuit used as the gate rather than the reader", is SERAC's thesis. Against the deployed arm B (RESULTS.md §7), EKP trades semantic and alias reach for lower false-fire. That is not clearly better, and the concept's own text already calls it an "evolution of arm B".
verdicts.salvage:
Drop both the Engram brand and the relaunch framing. Ship EKP as what it is: a hash-first, GTE-fallback scope gate on deployed arm B. That means an exact normalised-subject hit is high-confidence presence, the whitened-GTE 0.90 gate stays as the alias and paraphrase fallback, and the base's o_old top-k rank is an extra AND-gate.

Then make the evaluation the contribution, not the triad. Concretely:
- **Stage 0 cohorts.** Replace CounterFact-only Stage 0 with alias and coreference cohorts: RippleEdits Subject Aliasing (2307.12976), UniEdit Subject Alias (2505.12345), pronoun or definite-description multi-turn prompts, and the 2609.29045 re-tokenization attack.
- **Pass bar.** Pre-register a bar against the published 32% string vs 99.3% learned alias coverage (2609.11063 SN13).
- **Displacement gate ablation.** Report the gate against an ATBias-style rank-constrained bias (2406.12468) at matched α, so the one possibly new piece (o_old-rank used as the firing gate rather than as a token filter) is isolated.
- **Positioning.** Position the result as SERAC (2206.06520) with an exact-plus-semantic scope and a lossless pointer counterfactual. The spine is the presence-provenance rescue (RESULTS §8), the repo's least-trodden claim per novelty-positioning.md.

If the team wants a genuine Engram relaunch, the only literature-honest version is the assessment's E0 δ*-site falsification (engram-graft-assessment.md §3). The papers predict it fails on a frozen base, so run it as a falsification, not as a thesis.

verdicts.objection: EKP can be built cheaply, but the "decisive" experiment can't decide anything, and the one expensive, risky part (serving) has the weakest estimate. (1) Stage 1 is tautological on this harness. probe_and_filter_counterfact keeps a record only when the base's argmax equals true_ids[0] (recall_mag.py:739-770). So o_old is rank 0 on every edit prompt and the displacement trigger (a) always fires: A4 equals A3 on efficacy by construction. CounterFact neighbours have different subjects, so the presence key never arms: NBR-keep equals A0 by construction. Paraphrases keep the subject string, so coverage is about 1. At alpha=force, efficacy equals the hit rate at every N, so "flat N=137->1105" is guaranteed. It does not test the shared-readout diagnosis, because A1 vs A3 changes key, value and site together, and pointer losslessness is already known (RESULTS §7, "delivery-exact = addressing by construction"). Kill criteria 3, 4, the second half of 5, and 7 can hardly fail. The concept admits the triad will saturate. Its only new mechanism, a per-position displacement trigger over a 64-token armed window, cannot be measured from cached last-position logits. Every risk that would actually discriminate is deferred until after go/no-go: coreference, aliases, substring collisions, displacement misfires in free generation, 35B behaviour (M4/M5). (2) The serving port runs against the repo's own serving design. integration_design.md §3b/§5b/§5d moved the store read to prefill only, specifically so decode stays static and graph-capturable. EKP needs work on every decode step: incremental detokenize and canonicalise, update the armed set, check whether o_old is in the top-5 of possibly vocab-parallel TP logits, match the object prefix, and make a rank-0 decision that is broadcast to the other ranks (README.md:173-176). That means either a GPU-to-CPU sync per step in the hot loop, or rebuilding the logic GPU-side in the captured sampler with static buffers. "Logits are already computed, so this is free" is not true. The deployed pointer code is outside the repo, and the in-repo serving docs describe the tap MVP, not the pointer. So the 1-2 week estimate has no grounding. (3) Measured against keeping the current system, the concept itself predicts kill 8 (A3 about equal to A2). The founding thesis it "retires" was already retired by the deployed below-the-line system (README.md:182-186, RESULTS §7). That makes this a key and trigger change on arm B, not a relaunch, and not clearly better.
verdicts.salvage: Treat EKP as an evolution of arm B (a hash-first key with GTE fallback plus an implicit trigger), not a relaunch. Make the go/no-go test something that can actually fail. (a) Cache full-sequence logits over multi-sentence free generations and multi-turn contexts, and measure the displacement trigger's per-position misfire rate inside the 64-token armed window. Include positions where o_old is not the gold slot, so the result is decoupled from the validity gate. (b) Move the discriminating cohorts into M0/M1, before any go decision: coreference/pronoun, offline Wikidata aliases, substring entities (Paris / Paris Hilton), same-subject other-relation templates, and common-token o_old. Fix the canonicaliser to NFD with mark stripping. (c) Before any research spend, run a 2-3 day serving spike inside minisgl-rdna4: put the per-step trigger in the sampler as GPU-side static [max_bs, max_armed] buffers under graph capture and TP=2, and measure TPOT overhead against the current prefill-only pointer. Kill the idea if the overhead is more than a few percent or a per-step host sync is required. (d) Rebuild the A2 arm and the rank-R gate from the missing scripts first, so the head-to-head is config-matched.

redteam.name: Engram Cartridge: text-keyed n-gram memory files linked per base, delivered at the output
redteam.thesis: The memory is a base-free file of hashed normalized-text word-n-gram rows, written in closed form with EngramEdit's ridge/frequency allocation solved in text space and holding exact object strings. Each frozen base only links the file to its tokenizer and gets a hit-gated sparse logit bias or pointer forcing at the output. That makes "one memory, any frozen model" a re-encode with no translator, and the Engram residual site becomes at most an optional per-base compiled backend that has to earn its place (assessment E0).

verdicts.objection:
The repo's own measurements leave only the KEY for this concept to change, and the repo already counts addressing as solved.

1. The value and delivery are the same as the deployed system. D-FORCE is the deployed arm B value path: exact object token-ids, emitted by the `_gen_ptr` logic (RESULTS §7 A/B/C bake-off; CAM_100_DISJOINT_RESULT "THE UNLOCK").

2. The portability mechanism is not new either. integration_design.md already recommends persisting string edits and rebuilding at boot because that is "tokenizer-portable". And the bake-off already calls arm B "base-agnostic and training-free" (RESULTS §7).

3. The thesis "one memory, any frozen model as a re-encode, no translator" is therefore already true of what is deployed. The relaunch reduces to swapping a whitened-GTE subject key for a lexical word-n-gram key. The repo's synthesis says addressing is SOLVED: below-gate 0/441, and the open limit is efficacy-at-scale in the shared out_proj readout (key-encoding §0(A),(D)). The pointer arm does not have that readout.

4. The three things that are new are each predicted, by repo measurements, to hurt rather than help:
   - **(a) The relation gate costs generality.** The R-row relation gate is a prompt-surface gate ANDed onto a subject hit. The repo measured that gating on prompt surface instead of store retrieval cuts generalization to 0.611–0.667, against 0.907–0.926 with a store-confidence gate (RESULTS §7 "Closing the gap"). The repo's 0.818 GEN-hit exists precisely because routing is subject-only (key-encoding §3.17).
   - **(b) Dropping the explicit subject span turns firing into a per-decode-step decision.** That decision is the failure the repo measured: always-on firing degenerates to "French French French…" (key-encoding §3.20). The best automatic rule, router seed-once, managed 9/12 (RESULTS §8). The deployed MVP avoids this by requiring an explicit subject (integration_design.md §3a/§7 risk #1).
   - **(c) Sub-span keys collide.** Last-token subject keys were not separable at M=32 (bind carry ~0.55). Pooling the full span and dropping relation-prefix context lifted it to ~0.74 (RESULTS §7 "How far does it scale"). Word 1-gram S-rows are the lexical analogue. Once the ridge negatives suppress them, the key collapses to exact full-subject match, which is arm B's explicit subject without GTE's alias tolerance.

5. The decisive experiment cannot discriminate. CounterFact neighbourhood prompts share the SAME relation and true object but name DIFFERENT subjects (cam/realedit.py:9). So the R-gate adds nothing on the locality cohort, and lexical S-keys separate subjects trivially. The concept's own expected_failure_mode concedes this.

6. The kill thresholds compare against the wrong baseline. They are benchmarked on A1, the out_proj tap plus logit-inject arm (0.55 and 0.876 solo, key-encoding §0(D)/§3.14), not on the deployed pointer. The pointer's CounterFact triad at N=441 has never been measured in this repo, so "better than the deployed system" is never actually tested.
verdicts.salvage:
Do not relaunch. Treat the cartridge as two arm-B add-ons: an edit-plane file format, and a (subject, relation)-scoped lexical key that sits in front of the deployed whitened-GTE pointer as a prefilter. Lexical hit OR GTE ≥ 0.90 fires the pointer, and the R-cue becomes a disambiguator used only when one subject has more than one live relation, never an AND gate on every fire. That closes online_api.md §1.2 without paying the §7 prompt-surface generality cost. Then rerun C1 against the right comparator under conditions where the key can matter:
1. Measure arm B's actual CounterFact triad at N=441/1105. That number is missing from the repo.
2. Add a span-free serving cohort: free-generation decode steps scored per step for false-fire (the §3.20 hazard).
3. Add same-subject/other-relation and alias cohorts.

Only if the lexical/hybrid key beats arm B by more than 0.05 on those cohorts should the text-space negative-row ridge allocation be written up as its contribution. That contribution would be an offline false-fire calibrator; it is not a new memory thesis.

verdicts.objection:
The relaunch keeps none of the Engram mechanism that the literature actually supports, and the parts it does keep are already published or already deployed. Every positive Engram result has a backbone that was trained to read the memory: STAPLE trains the backbone for about 200B tokens, EngramEdit runs only on LongCat-Flash-Lite with natively pretrained n-gram embeddings, User-as-Engram runs on an Engram model, and 2608.17050 trains a reader per target. The cartridge drops learned values, early fusion and the context gate, so that evidence base gives it no support at all.

What is left is three things, none of them new:
1. A tokenizer-agnostic, NFKC-normalized word-n-gram hash key. 2608.17050 already publishes essentially this design.
2. A "text-space EngramEdit allocation". In EngramEdit, B holds d-dimensional delta* targets. With B set to binary 0/1 per fact, the solve becomes an ordinary ridge classifier on bag-of-n-grams features.
3. Exact-id forcing or a sparse logit bias at the output. That is the deployed arm-B pointer, and in mechanism it is SERAC: a black-box base wrapped with an explicit text edit cache and a scope classifier that overrides the output. Here SERAC's trained scope classifier is swapped for a weaker lexical one.

SERAC already found that hard out-of-scope inputs ("Who is the UK deputy PM?") are the bottleneck even for a trained cross-encoder. That is exactly the same-subject, other-relation case the R-row gate has to solve.

The decisive experiment also runs on CounterFact. On that benchmark a lexical subject trigger succeeds by construction: paraphrases keep the subject and neighbors name other subjects. The benchmarks built to expose this are CounterFact+ (which prepends the edit, subject included, to every neighborhood prompt, so a W=64-word window scan fires on all of them), RippleEdits (subject aliasing, compositionality) and MQuAKE (subject not named). None of them is in the plan. The delivery kill criteria benchmark against A1, the out_proj inject at 0.55. The real incumbent is arm B, and FORCE-mode efficacy equals fire rate, the same as arm B.

The only possible outcome is therefore the one the concept itself names in kill criterion 7: a key swap inside arm B, not a new core thesis.
verdicts.salvage:
Do not relaunch. Take the concept's own kill criterion 7 as the outcome from the start, and fold the text-hash key into the deployed arm B as a serving key option. Its real benefits are no GTE forward, no whitening statistics, no explicit subject span, an exact presence bit, and exact delete.

Make the decisive test the one the literature says lexical keys fail, not CounterFact alone. Run it on:
- CounterFact+ prefixed-neighbor prompts (2305.17553);
- a same-subject, other-relation cohort, which is SERAC's hard out-of-scope case;
- RippleEdits subject aliasing and MQuAKE subject-absent hops.

Compare against arm B (whitened GTE), SERAC with an embedding scope classifier, and gated IKE/RAG. Report the result as "SERAC-style black-box editor with a lexical-hash scope and exact-id pointer delivery", with 2608.17050 credited for the key.

A relaunch under the Engram name would need a positive E0: a frozen-base delta* at an early site beating the pointer. Both the literature and the repo's ~0.7 site wall predict it will fail.

verdicts.objection:
The cartridge can be built cheaply on this hardware. The trouble is that the decisive experiment C1 is not decisive, and the one thing that would make this a relaunch rather than a key swap is never tested by it.

(1) Most of the kill criteria pass almost by construction.
- D-FORCE emits stored ids, so efficacy equals fire rate. `_gen_ptr` span_exact compares the emitted gold ids with gold (recall_mag.py:2419-2438), so multi-token kill 9 can only catch a linking bug.
- SOFT is a constant α added to cached last-position logits. Scale kill 4 therefore cannot fire unless key fire rate decays.
- Portability kill 6 is guaranteed because the key never touches the base. The only cross-base variance comes from the different validity-gated subsets per base, which is a confound, not a test.
- Kill 7 has rigged escape hatches. The "retokenization-bypass" advantage is measured against a token-id 2-gram strawman, but the deployed arm B key is already whitened GTE over subject text (RESULTS §7 bake-off), so it is just as immune. The "subject-span-free" advantage is scored against A3, which is handed the harness span.
- The concept itself predicts that CounterFact is easy (its expected_failure_mode).

(2) "One memory, any frozen model, no translator" is already a property of the deployed system. Arm B is a "base-agnostic, training-free" key with a lossless id value (RESULTS §7). Edits carry the object string (online_api.md §1.1), so re-tokenizing per base is trivial. M2 re-proves something the system already has.

(3) The real new capability is span-free window scanning. That is exactly what breaks in serving, and C1 cannot see it. In the harness every prompt ends at the answer point. In serving the repo has shown that delivery must be answer-span-scoped: always-on injection degenerates into "French French French…". An automatic answer-span detector is listed as open (key-encoding §3.20); seed-once gets 9/12 (§3.28).
- A 64-word window that fires whenever subject and relation-cue n-grams co-occur gives FORCE no rule for *when* to emit. Examples: chat-template first tokens, subject mentions that are not questions, multi-fact long contexts.
- The concept names this hazard but neither the decisive experiment nor the kill criteria measure it. M6 (porting into the 35B MoE minisgl engine) only comes after the gates pass.

So C1 can come back all-green while saying nothing about whether this beats keeping arm B. Under the default rule, the concept is not clearly better than the current system.
verdicts.salvage:
Do not relaunch. Fold the normalized-text n-gram hash and the (subject, relation) presence gate into arm B as a key and gate option, and redesign the decisive experiment around the one property arm B lacks: serving with no subject span and no known answer point.

Concretely:
- Run on the deployed 35B MoE through minisgl at TP=2, not on HF 3-4B bases.
- Use a free-form chat and long-context cohort. It should contain answer-point questions, subject mentions that are not questions, same-subject other-relation prompts, and multi-fact contexts.
- Measure false-force rate per turn, correct-force rate, and fluency.
- Compare four arms:
  - arm B with an explicit subject (the oracle);
  - arm B with an automatic span picker (NER or last noun phrase) feeding the GTE key;
  - the cartridge's window scan with an explicit answer-point detector, which must be specified;
  - cartridge-gated RAG.
- Drop the rigged comparisons: the token-id 2-gram strawman and the span-handed A3.
- Replace the tautological kills (pointer span-exact, cross-base parity, flat scale) with the key-only fire-rate against A2's oracle ~1.0.

Promote the cartridge to a core thesis only if window-scan plus answer-point detection beats arm B with an auto-span picker on false-force rate at equal correct-force rate in serving.

redteam.name: Read-Port Retrofit (Mode B): a co-trained editable n-gram memory for a small open checkpoint
redteam.thesis: The repo's ~0.7 residual ceiling is plausibly a frozen circuit that never learned to read an additive channel. A one-time, cheap "world-swap" retrofit (0.05 to 2B tokens) of a small open checkpoint (Qwen3-4B-Base or Qwen3-1.7B-Base) should teach its backbone to read a hashed n-gram table. After that the backbone is frozen for good, and EngramEdit-style delta*+ridge writes should exceed the repo's frozen-base escapes: above the 0.88 solo logit-inject ceiling and above the 0.565 efficacy at N=441, with pointer-level locality. If they do not, the wall belongs to the site and not to frozen-ness. key-encoding §0(C) asserts that already but has never tested it with a trained backbone.

verdicts.objection:
The repo's own measurements already answer the relaunch's motivating question in a way that makes Mode B unable to beat the incumbent where it matters. The relaunch can only win on two axes, and repo walls that do not depend on frozen-ness predict failure on both.

1. Where the thesis comes from. The ~0.7 wall was shown to be a property of the injection site, not of frozen-ness. The same frozen base with the same value moved to the logit site went from 0.65 to 0.88 solo, with prior-reversion at 0.00 (key-encoding §3.14, §0(C)). K1 plus hard-gated logit inject then reached ~0.90 at N=137 with below-gate 0 (§3.16). So the pre-registered bar "solo >= 0.88" is parity with the existing frozen system, not "exceeding the frozen escapes".

2. Exactness. The deployed pointer delivers exact ids by construction: isolated 1.00, standing 4/4 span-exact (CAM_100_DISJOINT_RESULT "THE UNLOCK"). A learned r=512 row read out through a trained W_V and LoRA is exactly the lossy value regression the repo falsified four times: iso per-token 0.50, delivery 0/4, landing on adjacent subwords. Multi-token objects are ~46% of the bake-off set (RESULTS §7). So multi-token stays on the pointer for good, as the concept itself concedes.

3. Scale. The 0.565 at N=441 is the shared trained-readout limit of the tap/logit lineage (§0(D), §6g). The concept brings back a shared trained W_V and LoRA readout, and the pointer does not have that limit at all.

4. Generalisation and composition. Every trained readout the repo has built is relation-specific: novel-relation delivery 0.000 vs 0.77 (§3.23), and a 2-hop-trained tap ripples 0.85 on its own relation but 0.31 on a held-out one (scorecard F3). World-swap training on T-REx relations with CounterFact held out is the setup that predicts kill criterion 5 will fire. On integration, every activation write at every depth sits below RAG, early L3 garbles, and "a weight-space adapter trained the same way has nothing to gain above the cartridge" (scorecard; RESULTS §10; DIARY Phase 18).

Net: the frozen-vs-co-trained science question is genuinely untested in the repo. But every product claim beyond the pointer (scale, held-out relations, multi-token, ripple) runs into a measured wall that co-training was never shown to touch. The relaunch also drops the defining invariant before running the $0, training-free E0/E1 ladder that would test the wall directly.
verdicts.salvage:
Do not relaunch. First run the assessment's $0, training-free ladder on Qwen3-4B-Base, and re-measure the incumbent on that same base, because none of the repo's editing numbers were taken on it.

1. Run E0: a per-edit delta* bank at {embed, L2, L8, L16, L22/24}, presence-gated.
2. Run E1: raw-d rows vs a fixed projection vs a trained out_proj, from N=137 to 1105.
3. Re-measure K1 plus hard-gated logit inject and the pointer on Qwen3-4B-Base.

Fund a co-trained retrofit only if E0 sits at the ~0.7 site wall at every depth and E1 shows per-row values hold efficacy flat where the shared readout drops. Even then, run it as a cheap science probe and not as a relaunch:
- A2 vs A1 vs A3 at P_m only;
- held-out-relation efficacy as the primary metric (the §3.23/F3 signature);
- raw-d rows (W_V=I), so the shared-readout bottleneck is not reintroduced.

Keep the pointer as the product and as the permanent value path for multi-token objects. The parts most likely to survive are the hashed-key prefetch, the namespace salt and the presence bit. Fold those into the pointer system as arm D, with exact ids stored alongside any learned row.

verdicts.objection:
The relaunch's motivating premise is already answered in the literature, and in the opposite direction from the one the concept needs. The concept claims the repo's ~0.7 residual ceiling is "a frozen circuit that never learned to read an additive channel." Two lines of published work cut against that.

1. Frozen bases can be driven to about 100% efficacy by an optimised mid-layer perturbation at the last subject token, which is exactly the delta* that arm A0 uses. ROME does this on frozen GPT-J (CounterFact ES 99.9 / PS 99.1, cited in Larimar 2403.11901 Table 2). So the repo's 0.7 belongs to its own trained tap and readout (key-encoding §0(C)/(D)), not to frozen-ness. A0 at the L22 port will probably already clear the 0.88 solo bar, which makes the A0-vs-A2 contrast uninformative.

2. "Train the reader once, then write by closed-form least squares with no gradients and exact forget" is not new. It is Larimar (ICML 2024, 2403.11901): decoder fine-tuned once, memory written as M_i = M_{i-1} + C^-1 W^T (Z - W M), forget with alpha = -1, CounterFact ES 99.6 on GPT-J. Training adapters on a synthetic KB so a frozen 8B reads a keyed fact channel and can then be updated without retraining is KBLaM (2410.10450). "Fine-tune the model to apply supplied edits" is LTE (ACL 2024, 2402.11905), which is the concept's own A3 control. The concept and the repo cite none of these (grep finds only SERAC and GRACE, in multi-gate-steering.md).

The one Engram-specific ingredient, an early (L2) hashed lookup, is the part the literature says fails even in natively Engram-pretrained models. User-as-Engram (2606.19172) reports that writing to the early lookup drops recall to about a quarter, while late lookup is near-perfect. That leaves the late port: a keyed late-layer tap on a LoRA-softened base. That is GRACE, WISE or Larimar territory, and the concept itself names it as the most likely outcome (expected_failure_mode #2).

As a product it does not beat keeping the current system:
- The decision bars (0.88 solo, 0.75 at N=441) are set against the superseded PK-store / logit-inject arm, not the deployed pointer. The pointer delivers exactly by construction: RESULTS §4 0.917 with false-fire 0.00 at 48 multi-token objects; CAM_100_DISJOINT_RESULT 4/4 span-exact.
- The only axis where it could win is integration/ripple (M4), and that is deferred. Natively trained Engram editors are weak there: EngramEdit (2610.10533) MQuAKE-CoT 36.9/20.1/15.1 at 2/3/4 hops; User-as-Engram's table alone gets 23% indirect, and needs a shared LoRA to reach 41-44%, still below RAG's 54% at 34 facts.

Meanwhile the relaunch drops the defining invariants: frozen base, attach-anywhere portability, remove-the-organ, and the 35B deployment. On the evidence it becomes a late re-entry into the Larimar/KBLaM space on a 4B model.
verdicts.salvage:
Do not relaunch. Fold this into a bounded, pre-registered science arm that runs only if a cheap step passes, and fix three things.

1. Run arm A0 first, free. Use the ROME-style delta* at L22 on frozen Qwen3-4B-Base, stored as raw d_model rows keyed by a fingerprinted hash (this is the assessment's E0/E1). If A0 already clears 0.88 solo and holds efficacy flat from N=137 to 441, then frozen-ness was never the wall and Mode B has no scientific motivation. If A0 is near 0.7 while ROME-style weight edits are near 1.0, the wall is the repo's readout, which is again not a reason to retrain the base.

2. If a trained arm still runs, drop P_e at L2. User-as-Engram shows early-lookup writes fail even natively, so keep it at most as a negative control. Add Larimar, and a KBLaM-style synthetic-KB adapter on the same frozen base, as the reference arms that A2 must beat. Those two are the real prior art for "train once to read, then write without gradients."

3. Re-anchor the decision on the axis where the deployed pointer cannot compete. Move M4 (edit-ripple plus a MQuAKE subset vs the same-pass RAG oracle, RESULTS §10) into RETROFIT-0 as the primary pass/fail criterion. Benchmark efficacy and locality against the pointer, not the PK/logit-inject arm.

Only a ripple result above RAG on held-out relations, with an empty-table capability drop of 1 point or less, would justify dropping the frozen-base invariant. Otherwise keep the pointer system, and add the hashed presence-bit key to it as arm D, as engram-graft-assessment.md §3 already recommends.

verdicts.objection: RETROFIT-0 is not decisive, and the question it is meant to answer can be asked for about $0 before any of its spend. The relaunch rests on one claim: the ~0.7 wall comes from a frozen circuit that never learned to read an additive channel. The repo never measured that. What hit 0.7 was an amortised, trained, shared gated tap (key-encoding §3.7-3.9, which calls it "the robust reliability ceiling of a trained gated residual injection"). The repo then broke that tap's failures down into a weak value/readout against strong base priors and large object vocabularies (§3.10-3.12). A per-fact optimised delta* is a different object. It is the ROME v* recipe, which reaches roughly 100% efficacy on frozen bases in the ROME paper (from memory; not re-checked here). So arm A0 (frozen, delta* added to the residual, no table) will probably clear solo >=0.88 by itself at rho up to 1.0·||h|| (unverified on this base). If it does, the solo threshold cannot separate co-trained from frozen. The first kill criterion would then fire on "A2 within 0.05 of A0" and wrongly read a saturated frozen arm as "the wall is a property of the site." The failure branch is not decisive either. A miss at 200M tokens cannot tell a site wall from under-training: STAPLE needed about 200B tokens (2610.12599), and EngramEdit's base pretrained its 31.4B n-gram params natively (2601.21204). Each training-world row also sees only a few gradient updates in 200M tokens. Training is 1 seed, and kill margins are 0.05 against cohort noise of ±0.10 (key-encoding preamble). Every threshold (0.88, 0.565, keep 0.45, leak 0.075) was measured on Qwen3.5-4B with the bind/train_taps/pk_store pipeline that the proposal throws away. The arm A0 text names a reference, "the repo's conf-gated logit-inject result on this base", but no such Qwen3-4B-Base number exists. Rebuilding it needs the discarded code, and editability is known to shift across bases (0.69 vs 0.574, §3.11). Meanwhile the training-free E0/E1/E2 ladder in engram-graft-assessment.md §3 asks the same questions (does a per-fact row beat 0.7 frozen; is N=441 efficacy a shared-readout limit) using the existing harness. The proposal skips it in favour of $100-250+, a 50-125× jump over the project's ~$2 cloud scale, plus 1-2 weeks of new training code. On deployment: even a full pass yields a 4B dense model that cannot be retrofitted onto the deployed Qwen3.6-35B-A3B TP=2 (the proposal rules that out itself). That model would need a new minisgl model path with per-request conv state, prefix-cache invalidation on every write, and an autograd sidecar for writes. So the result does not improve the deployed system at all, which falls short of "clearly better than keeping the current system."
verdicts.salvage: Do not relaunch yet. Run engram-graft-assessment.md §3 E0→E1→E2 first, frozen and training-free, on BOTH Qwen3.5-4B (where every incumbent threshold was measured with the existing bind/logit-inject pipeline, so A0 has a calibrated same-base reference) and Qwen3-4B-Base. E0 is per-fact delta* rows keyed by a namespaced, fingerprinted subject-tail n-gram hash, gated by presence, at L2/L8/L16/L24. E1 compares raw-d rows with a fixed r=512 projection. E2 is ridge allocation. This costs about $0-5 and answers both premises directly: does an optimised per-fact row beat 0.7/0.88 on a frozen base, and does N=441 efficacy stay flat when there is no shared readout. Commit to Mode B only on a narrow pre-registered result: frozen E0/E2 is shown to stall (solo < 0.88, or efficacy falls more than 0.10 from N=137 to N=441), the stall localises to the channel and not to the row, and a 2-3 training-seed A2 vs A1 vs A3 contrast with thresholds re-measured on the retrofit base is then run. If frozen E0-E2 passes, fold the hash key, presence bit and per-row value into the deployed pointer system as arm D. That leaves the 35B TP=2 minisgl deployment untouched and drops the need to give up the frozen-base invariant.
